questions.question: A ball is thrown **horizontally** from a cliff of height $45\ \mathrm{m}$ at speed $15\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the time of flight, (b) the horizontal distance from the base of the cliff, (c) the speed of the ball just before impact.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Vertical free fall: $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{9} = 3\ \mathrm{s}$

**(b)** $x = v_0 t = 15 \times 3 = 45\ \mathrm{m}$

**(c)** $v_x = 15\ \mathrm{m/s}$, $v_y = gt = 30\ \mathrm{m/s}$

$v = \sqrt{v_x^2 + v_y^2} = \sqrt{225 + 900} = \sqrt{1125} = 15\sqrt{5} \approx 33.5\ \mathrm{m/s}$

questions.question: An object is launched **horizontally** with speed $v$ from a height $h$ above the ground. The object strikes the ground at angle $\theta$ below the horizontal. Express $\tan\theta$ in terms of $v$, $g$, and $h$.
questions.answer:
Horizontal speed is unchanged throughout: $v_x = v$

Vertical speed at impact (free fall from height $h$): $v_y = \sqrt{2gh}$

The impact angle satisfies $\tan\theta = v_y/v_x$, so:

$$\tan\theta = \frac{\sqrt{2gh}}{v}$$

Check limits: as $h \to 0$, $\theta \to 0°$ ✓; as $v \to 0$ (nearly dropped vertically), $\theta \to 90°$ ✓.

questions.question: A projectile is launched from level ground with initial speed $v$ at angle $\theta$ above the horizontal. Gravity is $g$. Derive the formula for the horizontal range $L$.
questions.answer:
Decompose: $v_x = v\cos\theta$, $v_{y0} = v\sin\theta$

**Time of flight** (vertical returns to zero):

$0 = v_{y0}t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 \Rightarrow T = \frac{2v\sin\theta}{g}$

**Range:**

$L = v_x \times T = v\cos\theta \cdot \frac{2v\sin\theta}{g} = \frac{2v^2\sin\theta\cos\theta}{g}$

$$L = \frac{v^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$$

Maximum range occurs at $\theta = 45°$ where $\sin 90° = 1$.

questions.question: A ball is launched from level ground at $20\ \mathrm{m/s}$ and $45°$ above horizontal. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the maximum height, (b) the total time of flight, (c) the range.
A ball launched from the ground at $30°$ above horizontal lands $20\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{m}$ away. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the initial speed, (b) the maximum height.

A stone is thrown at $60°$ above horizontal with speed $20\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the horizontal and vertical components of the initial velocity, (b) the maximum height, (c) the total time in the air.
Ball A is projected at $30°$ and ball B at $60°$ above horizontal, both from the same point and with the same initial speed $v$. Compare: (a) their ranges, (b) their maximum heights.
questions.answer:
**(a) Ranges:**

$R_A = \dfrac{v^2 \sin 60°}{g}$, $\quad R_B = \dfrac{v^2 \sin 120°}{g} = \dfrac{v^2 \sin 60°}{g}$

$R_A = R_B$ — complementary angles ($30° + 60° = 90°$) give equal ranges.

**(b) Maximum heights:**

$H_A = \dfrac{v^2 \sin^2 30°}{2g} = \dfrac{v^2}{8g}$, $\quad H_B = \dfrac{v^2 \sin^2 60°}{2g} = \dfrac{3v^2}{8g}$

$H_B = 3H_A$ — ball B reaches three times the height of ball A.

questions.question: A cannonball is fired **horizontally** from a cliff $80\ \mathrm{m}$ high at speed $40\ \mathrm{m/s}$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the time to hit the ground, (b) the horizontal range, (c) the impact angle below horizontal, (d) the speed at impact.

A ball is thrown from level ground and reaches its maximum height of $20\ \mathrm{m}$ at $t = 2\ \mathrm{s}$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the initial vertical speed, (b) the total time of flight, (c) the initial horizontal speed if the total range is $60\ \mathrm{m}$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** At maximum height $v_y = 0$: $v_{y0} = g t_{\text{up}} = 10 \times 2 = 20\ \mathrm{m/s}$

Check: $H = v_{y0} t - \frac{1}{2}g t^2 = 40 - 20 = 20\ \mathrm{m}$ ✓

**(b)** $T = 2 t_{\text{up}} = 4\ \mathrm{s}$

**(c)** $v_x = R/T = 60/4 = 15\ \mathrm{m/s}$

Launch speed: $v_0 = \sqrt{15^2 + 20^2} = \sqrt{625} = 25\ \mathrm{m/s}$

questions.question: An object is launched **horizontally** with speed $v$ from a cliff of height $h$. Take the launch point as the origin with $x$ horizontal and $y$ upward. A slope descends from the launch point at angle $\theta$ below horizontal (i.e., $y = -x\tan\theta$). Find the $x$-coordinate where the object lands on the slope.
questions.answer:
Trajectory: $x = vt$, $y = -\tfrac{1}{2}gt^2$

On the slope: $y = -x\tan\theta$

Substitute $x = vt$: $-\tfrac{1}{2}gt^2 = -vt\tan\theta$

Divide both sides by $t$ (non-zero): $\tfrac{1}{2}gt = v\tan\theta \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{2v\tan\theta}{g}$

Landing $x$-coordinate:

$$x = vt = \frac{2v^2\tan\theta}{g}$$

As a check: when $\theta \to 0$ (flat ground) $x \to 0$, meaning the object never lands on the slope ✓.
